events.description: CIA memo laying out policy options for dealing with Usama Bin Ladin: continue the current plan, a tribal capture raid, a US military cruise missile strike, and other options.

CIA paper circulated setting out the range of options available to US policymakers for addressing the Usama Bin Ladin problem: continue current plan, tribal raid, ambush, cruise missile strike, and others.
Option for simultaneous US military cruise missile strikes on residences among which Bin Ladin shuffles, with the CIA providing location data.

key_claims: In November 1998 the CIA saw its current plan to bring Bin Ladin to justice as reactive and unlikely to succeed.
The CIA's tribal assets preferred a raid on a single house to an ambush on a convoy because it was less likely to alert nearby Taliban security forces.
A simultaneous cruise missile strike on Bin Ladin's residences was seen as having a high chance of success if he was in one of them, but high risk to noncombatants.
The memo shows a US military strike option, and possible use of Masood's agent network, were under consideration.
